I'm the sort of person that should love an open game like this. I loved Morrowind, I loved Warband, and I've played games just like this on Kongregate back in the day (more recommendations are very welcome!). But wow... this just completely misses for me.

There's almost entirely no sound at all. No music, no sfx. You just right click areas to do stuff, rather than feeling like you're actually playing a game. There's no quests, and no story. 

So far, I walk over to the iron, mine the iron, walk to town to sell, buy some stuff for my outpost, walk to outpost, wait for build, then walk back to iron, repeat. That loop takes like 15 minutes, and considering you just right click on the map to move, almost the ENTIRE 15 minutes is literally just me staring at the screen do it's thing, with zero input. Realistically, this is almost an idler game. However, if you do in fact idle and go AFK, some random little thing will attack you, and since you don't give inputs (or it's too strong) you just lose. Losing "can" be as simple as being injured and needing to hobble back to town, or, as in my one case, you're unconscious, with no food or medicine, so you can't do anything at all to help yourself, and you just die. Gameover, because it's permadeath. So you're forced to sit there watching the painfully long walk, the extremely painfully long mining process, etc. I'm sure there's good elements to this game, it looks super promising, but WOW it's boring to actually sit through, and you MUST sit through it, or else keep making backup saves in case it goes bad.

I'm still really wanting to get into it, because I can see there's a gem here, but it's a diamond in the rough... a lot of rough... and I just don't want to subject myself to painfully boring torturously bad gameplay, just for that little nugget of goodness.

I really did try to love Kenshi. I watched ambiguous amphibian's playthroughs, watched a few hours worths of tips and tricks for noobs and none of it helped. Here's a couple of gripes that I have only having played an hour(mainly cuz I wanted to give myself the choice of refunding).

1st gripe:
If you're planning to play this game with a controller(or on a steam deck in my case), don't bother. All the tutorials and help this game gives you all assume you're playing on a keyboard. I'm no stranger to weird and clunky controls clearly meant for a keyboard and haphazardly being mapped to a controller, but this one just takes the cake. If you're forced to play on a controller on this game, you're basically screwed. Even moreso than the people who play this game on their pc. 

2nd gripe:
The game is very unintuitive. Now I've played some hella unintuitive games before(funger & funger 2, coe 5, and rimworld), but this one just takes it to a whole nother level that is frankly unfun.

When I try to form up a squad(like the tutorial blurb told me to), I get shot with a 6K price tag from john gunsmith. When I finally stumble unto the merchant after looking at a barren dessert and 30 minutes of fighting with the controls, the funds that I started as a wanderer may as well have been 0. When I try to build a small shack(cuz that's what the very first tutorial blurb i read outside of the pc controls ones said I needed to do to build a research bench), I get hit with "it's too close to a town", "this building needs 15K", and when I manage to find a spot it required 5 building materials that cost an arm and a leg outside where there's literally nothing. 

All this work just to access the very first concept the game taught me which was a research bench. I am sure it's better on pc, but labelling this game as "playable" on the steam deck oled is just false.

In conclusion, I really did want to give this game a chance. The community around it has made some amazing content and has told …

Ah, Kenshi.  I purchased this game after watching numerous Youtube videos of people doing their own creative / fun "runs" (such as a slave to business owner run, or a farming run, etc).  Each looked pretty neat, and as an avid Rimworld fan I thought "Hey, this is sort of like Rimworld but in third person 3d!".  Next steam sale, I excitedly hit purchase.

Well, I stand here now having installed the game and tried it for myself, and... "underwhelmed" doesn't do it justice.  Have you ever played really old MMO's, like EverQuest or DAOC?  Imagine hopping back in now, same graphics and all, and there was no tutorial or training missions to at least familiarize yourself with the controls.  Great, I did it to myself again, I purchased yet another game where I'm expected to watch hours of Youtube videos for stuff that the game itself refuses to teach.

There seems like there's potential here, if you want a super sandboxy open world type thing where there isn't any sort of story, plot, or world events.  It does seem to be one of those "Everything and the kitchen sink, too" sort of games, where if you have an idea - you can accomplish it.  I'm just typically not that creative, and need at least SOME degree of direction  to start playing a game. 

I may revise my review in the future if I give it another try, but I fear that this may be one of those games that's going to be more interesting to watch other people play, than to actually play myself.  Maybe I'm missing something, but my brain was practically SCREAMING at me, "Now what?".

# Kenshi — A Review

**Developer:** Lo-Fi Games | **Genre:** Open-World Sandbox RPG | **Platform:** PC

---

There is a moment early in Kenshi — maybe your third or fourth hour in — where you realize the game is never going to hold your hand. Your character has just been beaten unconscious by a wandering band of bandits, left bleeding in the dirt of a sun-scorched wasteland, with no quest marker telling you where to go and no tutorial pop-up offering consolation. And somehow, impossibly, you can't wait to get back up.

Kenshi is not a game of questlines. It's a game of emergent stories — of being a shopkeeper and a thief, a lone wanderer and a slave, and eventually an entire community of people working together to one day erect a city in the wasteland. The game never scripted any of it. It just gave you a world and stepped back.

At its core, Kenshi is an open-world RPG with real-time strategy elements and no linear narrative, set in a post-apocalyptic world where survival is brutally difficult. You begin with no skills and struggle simply to stay alive, leveling up abilities through use — thievery by stealing, combat by fighting — and slowly recruiting others to grow your band.

Eventually it becomes a surprisingly effective management game as you research technologies, construct buildings, and assign your people long lists of automated tasks — mining, farming, construction. The scope of what you can build toward is staggering. The path to get there is unforgiving.

That difficulty is the game's defining trait and its biggest barrier. The concept of a free-roaming RPG where you craft your own story is always intriguing, and the world is vast and impressive for a small indie project, but the game does a poor job of communicating its intricate systems to new players. There is no onboarding. You are expected to fail, learn, and try again. Whether that sounds like a feature or a flaw will determine whether Kenshi is for you.

cohorts.summary: Players entering the world find themselves dropped into danger without guidance or hand-holding.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the opening hours as unguided and lacking a tutorial, dropping players into a dangerous world without direction.

citations.review_text:
As far as RPGs go, Kenshi’s versatility is nearly unmatched. It feels less like a game built around one genre and more like a game that keeps absorbing the best ideas from others.

Love isometric RPGs like Wasteland or Pillars of Eternity? Kenshi gives you the freedom, systems and party management you’d expect, but drops you into a world that refuses to revolve around your story. Prefer colony sims like RimWorld or Stranded: Alien Dawn? You’ll find similarly deep mechanics, except your colony exists within a much larger, more dangerous and politically complicated world. Enjoy the environmental storytelling of Elden Ring? Kenshi tells its story through ruins, scars, factions and the things you discover when you wander somewhere you were never meant to survive.

There’s a satisfying grind and progression system reminiscent of RuneScape, minus the shackles of an MMO. There’s a dynamic trade economy, faction politics, base-building, slavery, warfare, exploration and even faction creation. And if you want multiplayer, there’s apparently a mod for that, too.

You get the point: Kenshi is extraordinarily versatile. It can become the game you want it to be.

But that flexibility comes at a cost.

Kenshi does not hold your hand. Not even a little.

You’ll be confused. You’ll be directionless. You’ll get beaten half to death by starving bandits, enslaved, robbed, eaten or otherwise reminded that you are not the protagonist of this world. When you begin, you’re so weak and unequipped that even surviving can feel like an accomplishment. I wouldn’t blame anyone for falling off within the first hour.

That initial frustration is the barrier. It is also the point.

Because Kenshi isn’t interested in giving you a heroic journey. It gives you a starting condition: a nobody with no money, no power and no guarantee that tomorrow will be better than today. Your story only begins once you figure out how to survive long enough to write it.

Eventually, the confusion starts to give way to…

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Mid-game adventurers rely heavily on community mods to manage difficult mechanics and rough pathfinding.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a steep learning curve and a severe lack of an in-game tutorial or direction for new players.

citations.review_text:
Kenshi is a surprisingly deep and engaging game. Great progression that's individual for every character, (although brutally difficult in the beginning), a dauntingly huge map with an absurdly huge amount of choices for where to go.

I do however have 2 negatives to bring up. With the Sci-Fi setting not having any kind of firearms is a hugely missed opportunity and feels like they should be there, but it's missing. And for new players there's a lack of direction and tutorial in my opinion. You're thrown into the world and get a figurative pat on the back and a "You're out here now, good luck!".

Some more explained details on the world, the in game mechanics and a more interactive tutorial wouldn't go amiss. But besides these 2 things I don't really have any complaints about it, except that I would personally like if the dialogue was voice acted. It does what it's supposed to incredibly well, the mod support is amazing with many fun additions you can throw into the game quite easily.

I was a bit sceptical at first since the gameplay looked more action oriented than it is, and the game doesn't have controller support. But a good way to describe the controls is Kotor, but with less combat options, base building and a larger party system.

Overall I give Kenshi 8.5/10. If guns (natively, not through mods), a longer and interactive tutorial, and voice acting are added it'll easily become a full 10/10!

There is a very steep learning curve and I'm still figuring it out with systems I haven't even touched yet, but I can say this game has an insane amount of depth to it along with some jank. The leveling system is unique in that you have skill levels, not character levels that increase according to where those stats are relative to whatever you are fighting/doing. The cool part is that you can manipulate this with various temporary stat buffs/debuffs. So it becomes a balancing act of how can I game the system for maximum stat gains without dying or being too inefficient. 

There are plenty of things that might seem like a negative or bad, like losing a limb or getting knocked out, enslaved, shotting squamates, etc, but you can game that for gain as well. 

Learning how things work and progression feels really rewarding, worth a try if you are on the fence.

Kenshi is the only game where being completely demolished qualifies as character growth.
You begin as weak as a wet paper towel, get mugged by homeless people trying to survive, captured by slavers, and gobbled up alive by fauna that could have come from a bad dream, yet still you wind up feeling:
“Yeah… one more hour.”
The absolute highlight is the tutorial.
In most games, the tutorial teaches you how to play.
In Kenshi, it’s literally just “good luck buddy,” throwing you into the desert without clothes.
10/10, best stockholm syndrome simulation.

I always struggle to review games like this, because the community is amazing and consistently releases new content and mods for this game. With that, I'll just be touching on the vanilla release, as with mods you can make it into whatever you want.

So Kenshi, what is it? It's a squad based open world game with a focus on community, allowing you to build your own structures, towns, and even empire. Unlike most other games of this nature, theres a huge focus on individual's rather than hero units or trainable soldiers. Your main team will be your main team for a majority of your sessions. I found it quite difficult to manage more than 3 squads at a time, 2 exploration teams and a 3rd to run and guard the base. This works well and allows you to limit the size of your operation to whatever you personally find managable.

Kenshi is a real time strategy, so you wont be influencing fights directly as much as youll be managing squad macro and keeping your people alive and healthy. The main hurdle when starting is learning that you're MEANT to get your ass kicked a few times. It's just counterintuitive and hard to learn. 

I have nothing but nice things to say about this janky buggy mess, I adore it and if you put the time in you might as well. New players would probably benifet from a tutorial start, but I'm not sure Kenshi even cares if you play it. Its a desolate world that would keep on scrapping by, with or without you. The ancient robots, ruins and sparse wastes hold several worlds worth of lore and story just waiting to be found. The lore is probably the best part of Kenshi, realizing this world is much older and much more complicated than you ever imagined. Strong 8/10 from me.

Kenshi is the only game where being completely demolished qualifies as character growth.
You begin as weak as a wet paper towel, get mugged by homeless people trying to survive, captured by slavers, and gobbled up alive by fauna that could have come from a bad dream, yet still you wind up feeling:
“Yeah… one more hour.”
The absolute highlight is the tutorial.
In most games, the tutorial teaches you how to play.
In Kenshi, it’s literally just “good luck buddy,” throwing you into the desert without clothes.
10/10, best stockholm syndrome simulation.

claims.claim: Reviewers rely on the extensive modding community and Steam Workshop to fix bugs, improve performance, and add quality-of-life adjustments.

citations.review_text: Please flesh out the automation a bit more, I highly recommend officially adopting the kenshi extension module that the modding community uses and the fixes they provide, there is no point in not accepting their contribution. By making the modding more integrated and unified, you can more easily provide a surface for extensions, like minecraft does with its mod authors, your aim is to effectively provide an ontology. The current hierarchy of your object graph is already very good in structure, refinements exist primarily as performance improvement, if you ran this in my companies custom ETCS (Entity Tag Component System) runtime, you could see events updating on the order of 10 million events per second +, as the system retains partial order over type graphs for you through C++ meta templating (CRTP). Since we are considering releasing our engine under open source (LGPL), you may be in for an interesting surprise in the future! I'll update this once its released, and if your interested, you can use it (as it is open source).
This game is AWESOME. I never find games that hold my attention for more than 2 weeks, but I've been playing this for months. A bit unoptimized, but mods fix this!

Kenshi is definitely one of those games that you don't realize how fun it is until you play. The in game world is vast and unique. It definitely keeps the gameplay refreshing as you travel around. I personally love the health / combat system, and I feel like skill leveling is balanced perfectly. Skills don't level too fast but are just fast enough for you to feel like progress is happening.  The steam workshop and nexus both host a massive selection of well-made mods to tweak the game as you'd like, and I've seen some pretty amazing things recently on that front. The performance out-of-the-box is mildly annoying but it can be mitigated with a few mods.

There’s really nothing else quite like it. Starting with a handful of useless nobodies and eventually building a powerful squad, a functioning base, and enough confidence to fight entire factions is incredibly satisfying. The freedom to play however you want is easily the game’s biggest strength, although the late game can feel a little empty once your squad is strong, your research is mostly complete, and you’ve run out of meaningful goals to chase.

That said, Kenshi is held together with duct tape and hope. The bugs can be frustrating, the pathfinding regularly makes terrible decisions, and managing a large squad sometimes feels like supervising a field trip where everyone is actively trying to get lost.

Mods also feel almost required for the best experience. Quality-of-life improvements, world-state mods, UI changes, and bug fixes smooth out a lot of rough edges that probably should have been handled by the base game.

Kenshi is clunky, ugly, confusing, and occasionally infuriating, but it is also genuinely unique and very hard to put down once it clicks.

It is an interesting take of a old western japanese steam punk medieval fantasy sword fantasy kung fu post apocalyptic sci fi setting. I've never seen someone mash this many ideas and just get a setting that feels cohesive and immersive. So the world building is good, now the gameplay, that needs work. Fortunately, this is one of the most moddable games out there, reducing raid frequencies, increasing NPCs, improving combat, rebalancing the economy... And now with Re Kenshi it is getting to another level again.

Incredible game when it functions correctly. Unfortunately I don't think I've had a single play session so far that wasn't interrupted for several minutes because of a bug or some jank ass feature. Corpes go flying miles away more often than not. Characters freeze and refuse to move until you reload. Any character doing an action autonomously stops when it's tile isn't being rendered, and the pathfinding rarely works as intended. There are also graphical issues and pop-in even at max settings, which I wouldn't usually mention but it does become a problem when you're trying to identify a building on the horizon.

What I find so frustrating is that the game is set up to give you control of large groups of units and lets you give them jobs to do without your input. This idea is completely worthless however when your stupid little ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ can't go 5 minutes without getting caught on the hitbox of a building.

There's so much potential here. Without considering bugs I would probably give it an 8.5/10. I just find myself frustrated too often to forgive.

I so want to recommend this game, it's fun, both playing in combat and trading, but the pathing AI is hot garbage. You will have to micromange any pathing beyond LOS or else you'll suddenly find they decided not to go the same path they have the last 10 times, but instead went on a new path or just decided to stand still and give up letting any skin spider or starving bandit wipe your entire squad. Not so bad when you have one squad or 1 person, but if you want to do any base building you may as well just have everyone sit in the middle of town twiddling their thumbs or else you'll come back to find them running in circles.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe a harsh, brutal, and unguided opening experience with a steep learning curve and slow progress, lacking hand-holding or tutorials.

citations.review_text:
An excellent game for those who want real hardcore and aren't afraid of very slow progress during gameplay. A brutal game that doesn't care about you. You can be a loner or have your own squad. Play as an assassin, an organization with goals you choose yourself (Role Play), be a trader, a vigilante, a warlord, a bounty hunter, a ranger organization that helps people, a drug lord, a slaver, an anti-slaver.

The game shines when you, after you become comfortable with the game, pick a role in the world of Kenshi.

Mods are strongly recommended
Very steep learning curve here. If you're into instant gratification, this one might not be for you. But, if you love working your ass off for a very satisfying payoff, this one is worth it.

THIS GAME IS AMAZING. I have never played something with so much sandbox freedom, so much space to move around, places to visit, goals to make, things to do. This game does not hold your hand, and they weren't kidding!

I first heard about Kenshi from Ssethzeentach and at first didn't think much of it. Though there came a time when I wanted to experience something new, and I remembered Kenshi with his high recommendation.

Ever since then I have loved playing this game, creating several different starts and living out different gameplay and stories, each unique and different from the last, even if it's on the same Moon of Kenshi. I too, recommend this game. Thank you Lo-Fi Games and Chris Hunt!

Are there any bugs? F*ck yeah, there's tons of em. Do i care? Nope. Does the game look like ass? It sure does. Do i care? Again, nope. Is the game janky as hell? It sure is. Yet again, do i care? No, i don't.
The first few hours are rough, because you have to get over all of the jank and unpolished things. 
But once you do, you won't be able to put it down.
There is NOTHING else like it. It's an RPG where you and your characters make the story.
You choose what you want to do. There are no quests, there are no markers, nothing.
Every playthrough is different and i urge you to not savescum. Roll with the punches, see what happens. Make it your own unique story. It will always be different.
I bought the game at full price shortly after a sale (bad timing on my part) because i watched a couple of videos and i thought it looked really cool and i was bored.
At first i regretted my purchase, to be quite honest.
But just a few hours later, i forgot all about it.
At this point, i feel like i robbed the dev.
Yes, you read that right. Dev. This was mostly developed by a single guy at first.
I can't wait for Kenshi 2. 
If you can get it in a sale and you are just slightly interested, BUY IT!
if it's not on sale and you are interested, BUY IT!
You won't regret it. Just give it more than 10 minutes. This isn't your typical AAA slop that hits you with dopamine injections every couple of minutes. 
Instead it rewards patience, creativity and persistence.
This is a game where you can truly create your own story in a massive sandbox.
But after a couple more hours, i didn't anymore

This games got to be one of the most in-depth reactive sandbox game I have encountered. It's a real gaming gem in the rough, I wish it had more features, but the amount of mods should cover most of that. There is  also Kenshi 2 that's gonna come up eventually so something to look forward to.

If you are on the fence about buying this game know these things, this doesn'g have a story or gameplay tutorial is not gonna help you at all, it's not sameful to look things up, and it's gonna be a very rough start, but once you start understanding how to get what you want, this game becomes very enloyble.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features extensive sandbox freedom with no mandatory story quests or markers, allowing players to create their own roles, build bases, and shape unique narratives.

citations.review_text:
Very steep learning curve, can feel overwhelming and a bit unfinished/unpolished but once you understand the basic mecanics it becomes a true sandbox with lore in which you can write your own story fully the way you want. 

For example, my frist few playthroughs were just surviving and getting by with a small gang trying to evade wildlife and slavers while looking for a safe place to setup a small base and a farm. The funny thing is I eventually figured out is that there is no safe place in the world of kenshi, when picking a location for a base the game forces you to consider which threats you are willing/can deal with and which you would rather avoid or cannot deal with. Playing as an adventurer / trader solo or with a small group without a base completely changes the gameplay as you will need to approach the game differently and will face different challanges and threats while traveling.

Fast forward to current playthorugh, I am waging war on one of the major factions, harrasing their patrols, inflitrating their cities, stealing tech and valuables, and kidnapping leaders and nobles to  destabilize their cities. The captives I then offer to their enemy (Shek & Skeletons) and that way I am forming alliances to form combined attacks and takeovers of their cities, one by one, untill the faction is completely shattered and no longer a threat. And after that its on to the next faction.

In case you are wondering, my campaign list is the Holy Nation > Smaller slaver factions and the slave market > the United Cities and the Traders Guild > Cannibals, bandits, hostile hive's, fogmen, thralls, and eventually march a massive army to crush CatLon and whatever is left of his empire.

Then there is the workshop with mods ranging from simple content additions to mods that completely overhaul the game, mechanics, combat, factions, and more lore. There are DLC quality and content level overhauls like Genesis for example!

Wrote this at 999.7 hours in and I dont even know what pl…

Honestly, been on the fence for a long time on this one.  Its a fun sandbox game where you see what the world has to offer and just enjoy playing.  No achievements to fuss over, no specific story to push you in one direction.  It has been a long time since I've played a game that was just a fun game to explore and enjoy.  It does have a few things I personally have issues with, but 90% of those can be solved by looking up a few mods the community has created to make the gameplay more suited to what you prefer.  Honestly a fun game and worth its price if you enjoy an open sandbox game.

For example with the modding, one issue I had was the speed in which you learn skills.  It felt a little slow to me, so I simply got a mod that doubled it.

Easily one of my top games of 2026 despite getting close to being 8 years old. I cannot wait for Kenshi 2 and whenever I decide to have a go at another playthrough.

Kenshi is an amazing open world game that really managed to sink its claws into me. If you love the idea of a top-down, open world sandbox game where the story of your playthrough is fully up to you: Wanna be a slave that plots to escape to freedom? A wandering trader who eventually makes a trading outpost? A warrior looking for the next big challenge? Pro Slavery? Anti-Slavery? 

All the choices are in the palm of your hand as you are fully free to focus on a chill/base building experience, go full murder/combat, explore and everywhere in between. You can further change the experience with the advanced settings, whether you want the game to be even more harsh than it can be or if you want it to be more chill. In either case the choice is fully yours. 

I have had plenty of memorable moments both when I was playing with just my MC and when I finally got around to recruiting people both for combat and for building a base. The game runs smooth like butter even at 4K and with visual mods. Speaking of mods you can further enhance the experience with the amazing visual, performance enhancing & QoL mods the community has created over the years. Feel free to look through my mod list if you want some ideas of what you can add to the game.

Overall between the base game and what the community has built, Kenshi is an amazing open world sandbox game that I think anyone interested in these styles of games should give a try. The game might kick your ass but you will have a grand time whether you are getting yours handed to you, doing the handing, just exploring or building a base. Kenshi will surely have something you can do that appeals to your style of gameplay in an open world game.
